title: Hario V60 brewing guide
scope: One hot cup in a conventional plastic Hario V60 02 with classic matching 02 cone paper; app operationalization of Hario UK's September 2026 recipe, with distinct creator and iced variants.

sources.title: How to Brew Coffee with Hario V60 Coffee Dripper (September 16, 2026)
supports: 15 g coffee and 250 g brew-water input, medium grind, 92–94 °C
45 g bloom, 30–45-second wait, cumulative 150 g and 250 g
Overall 150–180 seconds including bloom; texture, preparation and taste adjustments

sources.title: Intermediate V60 Brew Guide
supports: V60 02 with matching 02 paper; rinse and discard rinse water, tare, dose 15 g, retare
92–96 °C, wet all grounds, wait about 30 seconds, slow circular pour to 250 g
2.5-minute wording appears in drain step without an explicit clock origin

sources.title: V60 Plastic Coffee Dripper 01
supports: Size 01 is labeled 1–2 cups; no universal cup volume inferred

sources.title: V60 Plastic Coffee Dripper 02 - Classic Colors
supports: Size 02 is labeled 1–4 cups; conical shape and spiral ridges; clear plastic model material

sources.title: V60 Plastic Coffee Dripper 03
supports: Size 03 is labeled 1–6 cups; no numeric liquid-fill capacity inferred

sources.title: V60 Meteor Filters 50ct Box
supports: Match paper and dripper sizes; paper regulates flow and contact time
Meteor is described as faster-flow than classic paper; no independent permeability test claimed

sources.title: Hario V60 Recipe & Interview with Hario Ambassador Scott Rao
sources.author_or_organization: Scott Rao, published by Hario UK
supports: Plastic V60, 20 g dose, 330 mL total water and 97 °C; source's 97 °F is an obvious conflicting typo
60 mL bloom with aggressive spin; wait 40 seconds; 200 mL cumulative then gentle spin
Wait until about 70 percent drained before final 330 mL target; typical 240–270 seconds

sources.title: Hario V60 Recipe & Interview with Hario Ambassador Tetsu Kasuya
sources.author_or_organization: Tetsu Kasuya, published by Hario UK
supports: 20 g coarse coffee, 300 mL water at 92 °C
Added 50/70/60/60/60 mL at elapsed 0/45/90/130/160 seconds; remove at 210 seconds
Creator describes modified ceramic dripper's slower flow and 4:6 taste framework

sources.title: Japanese brew guide on iced pour-over coffee
supports: 16 g medium-fine coffee, 150 g hot water at 91 °C, 70 g brew ice
Added 40/60/50 g at 0/40/70 seconds, each about ten seconds; approximately 130-second brew
Melt original ice before serving over additional ice; English page leaves V60 size unspecified

sources.title: Encore ESP Operations Manual, January 2023 v1.0, page 5
supports: Exact Encore ESP model's suggested Hario V60 starting setting is 25
Settings are starting points that can vary with recipe and taste

sources.title: V60 Coffee Server and Dripper Starter Set manual
supports: Manual link verified on Hario USA starter-set product page, but PDF fetch returned HTTP 403; no manual safety or cleaning instructions verified

recipe.name: App operationalization of Hario UK's September 2026 one-cup recipe
recipe.grind_description: Medium, resembling granulated sugar; tune for actual coffee and paper

expected_time_s.clock_start: First water touches coffee; explicit app convention for the source's overall time including bloom
expected_time_s.clock_end: Standing water drained and continuous outlet stream subsided; reference range, not automatic cutoff

recipe.completion_signal: No standing water remains above the bed and continuous flow has become occasional drops; remove dripper safely

steps.instruction: Fold seam, fit paper, rinse, discard rinse water.
steps.completion: Seated wet paper; empty, stable vessel.

steps.instruction: Add 15 g, level, zero assembly on scale.
Start clock at first water; wet bed with 45 g.

steps.why: App-selected lower end of published wait.
steps.completion: Wait elapsed; no fixed overall timestamp.

steps.instruction: Add 105 g in circles to 150 g total.

steps.why: Let bed drain before final pour.

steps.instruction: Add 100 g to 250 g total; avoid overflow.
Allow drainage, remove by handle, mix coffee.

variants.name: Hario older intermediate guide
variants.how_it_differs: 15 g/250 g, 92–96 °C, about 30-second bloom of unspecified mass, then continuous circular pour; 2.5-minute wording lacks explicit clock origin.

variants.name: Rao Hario interview recipe
variants.how_it_differs: 20 g in plastic V60, 97 °C, source 60/200/330 mL cumulative targets; aggressive bloom spin and brief gentle settling spins. Final pour follows about 70 percent drainage; typical total 240–270 seconds.

variants.name: Kasuya interview 4:6
variants.how_it_differs: 20 g coarse coffee, 300 mL at 92 °C; five source additions 50/70/60/60/60 mL at 0/45/90/130/160 seconds; removal at 210. Identify conventional versus modified ceramic geometry before implementation.

variants.name: Kurasu flash iced
variants.how_it_differs: 16 g, 150 g hot water at 91 °C plus 70 g brew ice; hot additions 40/60/50 g at 0/40/70 seconds, about ten seconds each. Approximate drawdown 130 seconds; melt brew ice before serving. Hot input ratio 1:9.375, hot water plus ice 1:13.75; neither is beverage yield.

variants.name: Other sizes, materials or paper
variants.how_it_differs: Use matching filter size and revalidate dose, pour behavior and drainage; cup labels are not universal volume capacities.

troubleshooting.check_first: Check matching seated paper, unobstructed outlet, receiver airflow and recent paper changes.
troubleshooting.adjustment: If still slow and harsh, grind slightly coarser; repeat consistent pouring.

troubleshooting.check_first: Confirm zero, dose, level bed and that water reaches grounds rather than paper edge.
troubleshooting.adjustment: Try slightly finer grind; change one variable before tasting again.

troubleshooting.check_first: Confirm recipe and equipment before diagnosing from elapsed time.
troubleshooting.adjustment: Try slightly coarser grind; maintain other inputs.

safety: Keep brewer and receiving vessel stable; leave room below rim and pause before overflow.
Keep hands clear of hot water; lift by handle and place dripper on a heat-resistant surface.
Cool before discarding paper and grounds; wash gently, rinse and dry.
Follow exact model's manual for dishwasher, microwave or heating use; those compatibilities were not verified in this pass.

app_audit.finding: V60 defaults are 1:16, 2.5x bloom, four post-bloom pulses, 93–96 °C, 150–210 seconds and medium-fine. This coherent app profile differs from both Hario publications.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Label defaults app-authored; if adopting selected research baseline, update its ratio, 3x bloom, two main additions, temperature, grind and timing together without overwriting named creator recipes.

app_audit.finding: V60 inherits STANDARD decaf policy subtracting 30 seconds; domain/BrewCalculator.kt:63 applies it. No reviewed V60 source establishes this universal shortcut.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Use NONE for V60; retain recipe and observational drainage, then tune for the actual beans.

app_audit.finding: V60 legacy plan has bloom countdown and manual pour only. Current legacy guidance is recipe-neutral, but does not provide a distinct finish-drainage action.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Add an observable drainage/serve step or explicit drained-before-finish cue without automatic finish deadlines.

app_audit.finding: Older official intermediate 15/250 continuous-pour recipe is already present with unspecified bloom mass and 92–96 °C. Its approximate 150-second total is clearer than the original source's drain-step wording.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Keep historical projection immutable; label total clock as app interpretation and create a distinct September 2026 baseline if adopted.

app_audit.finding: Audit claims older intermediate source matches about 2:30 total. That source places 2.5 minutes in drain step without clock origin. Rao and Kasuya rows also use grams for originally published millilitres.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Revise current audit conclusions to disclose time interpretation and unit normalization; preserve source snapshots.

app_audit.finding: Rao's 330 mL and Kasuya's 300 mL source water are stored as exact gram inputs; typed plans likewise normalize additions and cumulative targets.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Declare mass-based adaptations and retain original volumes, or obtain explicit mass evidence. Do not claim grams and millilitres are identical. Keep Rao's 97 °C; source's 97 °F is a conflicting typo.

app_audit.finding: Rao final observation has RANGE 240–270 seconds. BuiltInP1ExactStagePlanCatalog.kt:191 uses RANGE as a minimum advance constraint, holding completion until at least 240 seconds.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Separate advisory typical total-time range from minimum timing constraints; allow completion based on actual drainage.

app_audit.finding: Flash first pour has ten-second duration, second and third typed pours do not; source specifies about ten seconds for each. Catalog correctly separates 150 g water/70 g ice, both ratios and ice-melt completion.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Add approximate ten-second duration cues to second and third flash pours; preserve drainage and original-ice-melt observations.

app_audit.finding: Kasuya and flash retain BLOCK-V60-VARIANT; only canonical English has completed independent technical review. P1ExactGuidanceFactualErrata.kt contains no V60 correction branch.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Retain blockers until hardware variant evidence and review are resolved; catalog presence does not prove everyday-method, localization or release readiness.

app_audit.finding: Exact Encore ESP V60 starting setting 25 matches manufacturer manual page 5. Other V60 entries name models/burrs/calibration; generic decaf/process modifiers are still broad claims and were not independently verified here.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Retain verified Encore ESP point as model-specific; use descriptive baseline grind and avoid importing settings across grinders or named recipes. Review universal decaf/process modifiers separately.

app_audit.finding: All V60 profiles use BrewWaterMinusRetention(2.0); profile defaults similarly estimate output with a fixed 2 g/g apparent loss. Named Hario recipe explicitly leaves beverage output unresolved.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Keep output clearly estimated and optionally measured/calibrated; do not promise an exact cup mass or universal retention coefficient in the guide.

uncertainties: Hario starter-set manual https://global.hario.com/product/VCSD.pdf, product https://global.hario.com/product/coffee/dripper/VD.html and catalog https://global.hario.com/pdf2016/2016COFFEEcatalog.pdf returned HTTP 403; exact model cleaning/heating compatibility remains unverified.
Older Hario intermediate page leaves 2.5-minute clock origin ambiguous. Selected current recipe's clock at first water and 30-second wait after bloom pour are explicit app choices.
Rao and Kasuya interview quantities are millilitres, not independently verified gram targets; source clock placement around pouring/waiting is not fully explicit.
Kasuya discusses modified ceramic ribs but generic recipe header and shop link do not resolve every conventional versus Kasuya-model applicability claim.
Kurasu English source does not identify V60 size; brew-ice melt and drawdown are separate completion observations.
Only Encore ESP grinder setting was revalidated against its primary manual; remaining grinder settings and generic decaf/process adjustments need separate evidence review.
This is English research content, with no physical brewing, native device execution, localization review or release validation.
do_not_claim: One universal best V60 recipe or fixed finish deadline.
250 g poured water equals 250 g beverage, or all grounds retain exactly 2 g/g water.
A 02 dripper holds four full mugs simultaneously, or cup labels define a universal volume.
Rao's or Kasuya's mL quantities are exactly interchangeable with grams.
V60 decaf always needs a 30-second shorter brew or a fixed number of coarser grinder clicks.
Rao spin, Kasuya 4:6 pulse logic and Hario current recipe can be hybridized under creator attribution.
Flash brew's 150 g hot water plus 70 g ice guarantees 220 g beverage.
Source review proves a physical brew, approved translation, release readiness or exact grinder calibration.
